title: The page language code must be valid
summary: The lang attribute on the html element is not a real language code, so tools cannot use it. Replace it with a valid code such as en.
problem: The lang attribute on <html> holds a value that is not a valid language code, such as "english" instead of "en". Browsers and screen readers cannot match it to a language.
whoItAffects: Screen reader users, whose software chooses a voice from this code. With an invalid code it may fall back to the wrong voice. Translation tools and spell checkers cannot rely on it either.
whyItMatters: A wrong language code gives the same poor result as a missing one. This is a WCAG 3.1.1 failure at Level A, the baseline that accessibility regulations and procurement requirements commonly build on.
steps: Find the opening <html> tag in your template or theme.
Replace the lang value with a valid code from BCP 47: a two or three letter language code, such as en, fr or de.
Add a region subtag only if it matters, such as en-GB or pt-BR. Use hyphens, not underscores.
Do not write the language name, such as english, in the attribute.

howToCheck: View the page source and read the lang value on <html>. It should be a short code such as en or en-GB, not a language name or a made-up value.
